description: seam-beside-crossing-fuse's two cylinders with the turn 7e-6° past −90°: the turned seam meets the first wall 1.22e-7 either side of a point 1.22e-7 from the crossing vertex (0, R, 0), so the two seam crossings and the crossing vertex are three points 1.7e-7 and 2.4e-7 apart — between one vertex tolerance (1e-7) and the two that would keep their balls apart. The solid is the Steinmetz union of cross-cylinders-fuse, as at every turn. Arris failed here from 5.8e-6° to 1.1e-5° past ±90°, where the lateral offset is one to two tolerances, in two ways. It raised Fault::Split, 'a section edge of f1 ends at a node nothing else reaches': the seam's touch was resolved into its two crossings (ADR-0016), each a vertex of its own, and the two blocks between them and the crossing vertex, 1.7e-7 long, were dropped as boundary (found in plans/seam-parametrisation-faults step 4); the section vertices are now the components of their candidate points under 'the balls meet', and the three are one vertex (plans/c3-tolerance-apart step 2). It then failed L2 at that vertex: the seam ends at its touch and the ellipses at the crossing, 1.22e-7 apart in (u, v) on the turned wall, above the parametric tolerance. The vertex's point is now the seam's, an operand edge's, and a section edge's pcurve ends on the vertex's own (u, v) on each face — the seam's pave on the turned wall — its tolerance raised by the move (step 2b). The result is the body at −90°, the three points one vertex: features a tolerance apart are one feature

analytic.counts_differ: Open CASCADE builds its body at −90° here too, 9/15: the seam cut once, at the crossing vertex. It also cuts the section arc that runs through an ellipse's parameter origin, one more vertex and edge than Arris, whose edge range crosses the period once (E1), as in cross-cylinders-common
